key_insight: Detonation-sprayed hydroxyapatite coatings on Grade 2 titanium deliver the best tribological performance at intermediate O₂/C₂H₂ ratios, especially 3.0–3.3.
engineering_relevance: The study suggests a practical route to improve titanium implant wear resistance and physiological durability while supporting bioactivity and osseointegration.
method: Deposited hydroxyapatite on commercially pure Grade 2 Ti using detonation spraying.
Varied O₂/C₂H₂ ratio from 2.6 to 3.7 to tune coating structure and phase composition.
Compared tribological behavior in dry conditions and in Ringer’s solution.
evidence_signal: XRD showed mostly hydroxyapatite with some α-tricalcium phosphate, and wear testing found the lowest wear and best friction at O₂/C₂H₂ ratios of 3.0 and 3.3.
watch_item: High-temperature detonation spraying can introduce phase changes and coating heterogeneity, so process control is critical to avoid performance variability.
paper_title: STUDY OF TRIBOLOGICAL PROPERTIES OF BIOCOATINGS BY DETONATION SPRAYING METHOD
